greek: Εἶπεν δὲ κύριος πρὸς Μωυσῆν λέγων Εἴσελθε πρὸς Φαραω· ἐγὼ γὰρ ἐσκλήρυνα αὐτοῦ τὴν καρδίαν καὶ τῶν θεραπόντων αὐτοῦ, ἵνα ἑξῆς ἐπέλθῃ τὰ σημεῖα ταῦτα ἐπʼ αὐτούς·
hint: Moses is sent to Pharaoh again; the lord says he has hardened Pharaoh's heart so that these signs may come in succession.

notes.lemma: ἵνα ἑξῆς ἐπέλθῃ τὰ σημεῖα ταῦτα ἐπʼ αὐτούς
notes.text: That these signs may come upon them in order: the Hebrew has lĕmaʿan šitî ʾōtōtay ʾēlleh bĕqirbô, that I may set these my signs in his midst.
σκληρύνω, to harden: Middle Liddell's one translation, plain text, as at 9:12.

names.gloss: (Μωυσῆς, from Hebrew Mōšeh, which the Hebrew of 2:10 hears in māšâ, "to draw out")
(Φαραω, from Hebrew Parʿōh, from the Egyptian for "great house")

greek: ὅπως διηγήσησθε εἰς τὰ ὦτα τῶν τέκνων ὑμῶν καὶ τοῖς τέκνοις τῶν τέκνων ὑμῶν ὅσα ἐμπέπαιχα τοῖς Αἰγυπτίοις, καὶ τὰ σημεῖά μου, ἃ ἐποίησα ἐν αὐτοῖς, καὶ γνώσεσθε ὅτι ἐγὼ κύριος.
hint: The signs are to be told to children and grandchildren, so that they know he is the lord.

notes.text: What I have mocked the Egyptians, the perfect of ἐμπαίζω with the dative: the Hebrew has ʾēt ʾăšer hitʿallaltî bĕmiṣrayim, how I have dealt with Egypt.

notes.lemma: τῶν τέκνων ὑμῶν … τοῖς τέκνοις τῶν τέκνων ὑμῶν
notes.text: Of your children and to your children's children, plural: the Hebrew has binkā ûben-binkā, your son and your son's son, singular.
That I lord: a verbless clause, as the Hebrew kî-ʾănî YHWH.

greek: εἰσῆλθεν δὲ Μωυσῆς καὶ Ααρων ἐναντίον Φαραω καὶ εἶπαν αὐτῷ Τάδε λέγει κύριος ὁ θεὸς τῶν Εβραίων Ἕως τίνος οὐ βούλει ἐντραπῆναί με; ἐξαπόστειλον τὸν λαόν μου, ἵνα λατρεύσωσίν μοι.
hint: Moses and Aaron ask Pharaoh, in the name of the God of the Hebrews, how long he will refuse to yield.

notes.text: To turn toward me, ἐντρέπομαι with the accusative, to give heed to, respect: the Hebrew has lēʿānōt mippānāy, to humble yourself before me.
Until what: τίνος masculine, with χρόνου understood, as MorphGNT reads ἕως οὗ.

names.gloss: (Ααρων, from Hebrew ʾAhărōn, of uncertain meaning)
(Εβραῖος, from Hebrew ʿIbrî, usually connected with ʿēber, "the region beyond")

greek: ἐὰν δὲ μὴ θέλῃς σὺ ἐξαποστεῖλαι τὸν λαόν μου, ἰδοὺ ἐγὼ ἐπάγω ταύτην τὴν ὥραν αὔριον ἀκρίδα πολλὴν ἐπὶ πάντα τὰ ὅριά σου,
hint: If Pharaoh refuses, the lord will bring a great swarm of locusts across his borders tomorrow.

notes.text: At this hour: not in the Hebrew, which has only māḥār, tomorrow.
Much locust, the singular collective with πολύς: the Hebrew has ʾarbeh alone.
ἀκρίς, a locust: Middle Liddell's one translation, plain text.

greek: καὶ καλύψει τὴν ὄψιν τῆς γῆς, καὶ οὐ δυνήσῃ κατιδεῖν τὴν γῆν, καὶ κατέδεται πᾶν τὸ περισσὸν τῆς γῆς τὸ καταλειφθέν, ὃ κατέλιπεν ὑμῖν ἡ χάλαζα, καὶ κατέδεται πᾶν ξύλον τὸ φυόμενον ὑμῖν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς·
hint: The locusts will hide the ground and eat what the hail left, down to every tree.

greek: καὶ πλησθήσονταί σου αἱ οἰκίαι καὶ αἱ οἰκίαι τῶν θεραπόντων σου καὶ πᾶσαι αἱ οἰκίαι ἐν πάσῃ γῇ τῶν Αἰγυπτίων, ἃ οὐδέποτε ἑωράκασιν οἱ πατέρες σου οὐδὲ οἱ πρόπαπποι αὐτῶν ἀφʼ ἧς ἡμέρας γεγόνασιν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ἕως τῆς ἡμέρας ταύτης. καὶ ἐκκλίνας Μωυσῆς ἐξῆλθεν ἀπὸ Φαραω.
hint: The locusts will fill every house in Egypt, a sight unknown to Pharaoh's ancestors; Moses turns and leaves.

notes.text: Their great-grandfathers, πρόπαππος, Middle Liddell's one translation, plain text: the Hebrew has waʾăbôt ʾăbōtêkā, your fathers' fathers.
Moses, named: the Hebrew has wayyipen, he turned, with no name.

greek: καὶ λέγουσιν οἱ θεράποντες Φαραω πρὸς αὐτόν Ἕως τίνος ἔσται τοῦτο ἡμῖν σκῶλον; ἐξαπόστειλον τοὺς ἀνθρώπους, ὅπως λατρεύσωσιν τῷ θεῷ αὐτῶν· ἢ εἰδέναι βούλει ὅτι ἀπόλωλεν Αἴγυπτος;
hint: Pharaoh's servants urge him to let the men go and serve their God, since Egypt is already ruined.

notes.text: σκῶλον, not in Middle Liddell, which has only the masculine σκῶλος, a pointed stake: LSJ's stumblingblock, hindrance, citing this verse, for the Hebrew môqēš, a snare.
Their God: the Hebrew has ʾet-YHWH ʾĕlōhêhem, the LORD their God.
Or do you wish to know: the Hebrew has hăṭerem tēdaʿ, do you not yet know.
The second perfect of ἀπόλλυμι, which Middle Liddell gives with the middle: to perish utterly, and stand perished.

names.gloss: (Αἴγυπτος, the Greek name of the land; Hebrew Miṣrayim)

greek: καὶ ἀπέστρεψαν τόν τε Μωυσῆν καὶ Ααρων πρὸς Φαραω, καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Πορεύεσθε καὶ λατρεύσατε τῷ θεῷ ὑμῶν· τίνες δὲ καὶ τίνες εἰσὶν οἱ πορευόμενοι;
hint: Moses and Aaron are brought back; Pharaoh allows them to go and serve, but asks exactly who will go.

notes.text: They turned back, active and plural: the Hebrew has wayyûšab, was brought back, passive and singular.
Your God: the Hebrew has ʾet-YHWH ʾĕlōhêkem, the LORD your God.
Who and who, for the Hebrew mî wāmî.

greek: καὶ λέγει Μωυσῆς Σὺν τοῖς νεανίσκοις καὶ πρεσβυτέροις πορευσόμεθα, σὺν τοῖς υἱοῖς καὶ θυγατράσιν καὶ προβάτοις καὶ βουσὶν ἡμῶν· ἔστιν γὰρ ἑορτὴ κυρίου τοῦ θεοῦ ἡμῶν.
hint: Moses says everyone goes, young and old, sons and daughters, flocks and herds, for it is the lord's feast.

notes.text: νεανίσκος, a youth: Middle Liddell's one translation, plain text.
Of the lord our God: the Hebrew has ḥag-YHWH lānû, we have a feast of the LORD.
πρεσβύτερος, the comparative of πρέσβυς, under one article with νεανίσκοις.

greek: καὶ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς Ἔστω οὕτως, κύριος μεθʼ ὑμῶν· καθότι ἀποστέλλω ὑμᾶς, μὴ καὶ τὴν ἀποσκευὴν ὑμῶν; ἴδετε ὅτι πονηρία πρόκειται ὑμῖν.
hint: Pharaoh retorts that the lord would need to be with them if he let their households go, and sees evil intent.

μή opening a question that expects no, and καί adverbial, also.

notes.text: Except the sheep and the oxen, leave them behind: πλήν with the genitive, the preposition; the middle imperative, leave for yourselves.
The baggage, household: the Hebrew has ṭappĕkem, your little ones.

reading: and [[called|called, summoned, called to himself, invited|καλέω]] [[name:Φαραω]] [[name:Μωυσῆν]] and [[name:Ααρων]] [[saying|saying, speaking, declaring, calling by name, telling|λέγω]] [[go slowly|go slowly and walk, go and march, go by land, enter, proceed|βαδίζω]], [[work for hire|work for hire and pay and be in servitude and serve, be bound and enslaved to, serve, obey, render due|λατρεύω]] [[to lord|to lord, to master, to the one having power and authority over|κύριος]] [[to the God|to him who is God definitively, to the one the article marks out, to the known and the only|θεός]] of you; [[more than|more than, except, save and short of, save in respect, but, than, much like, only not, except that, save that, save so far as|πλήν]] [[of the things that walk forward|of the things that walk forward, of the cattle, of the flocks and herds, of the horses, of the small cattle, of the sheep|πρόβατον]] and [[of the bullocks|of the bullocks and bulls and oxen, of the cows, of the oxen, of the kine and cattle, of the ox-hide shields|βοῦς]] [[leave remaining for yourselves|leave remaining for yourselves, leave behind for yourselves, reserve for yourselves|ὑπολείπω]]; and [[the removal|the removal and riddance, the baggage, the household stuff, the ordure and filth|ἀποσκευή]] of you [[let run off|let run off, let run away, let run hard|ἀποτρέχω]] [[in the midst of|in the midst of, among, in common, along with, with, by means of|μετά + genitive]] of you.

greek: καὶ εἶπεν Μωυσῆς Ἀλλὰ καὶ σὺ δώσεις ἡμῖν ὁλοκαυτώματα καὶ θυσίας, ἃ ποιήσομεν κυρίῳ τῷ θεῷ ἡμῶν,
hint: Moses replies that Pharaoh himself will have to give them burnt offerings and sacrifices for the lord.

notes.text: You will give us burnt offerings and sacrifices: the Hebrew has tittēn bĕyādēnû zĕbāḥîm wĕʿōlōt, give into our hand sacrifices and burnt offerings, the other order.

reading: and [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told|λέγω]] [[name:Μωυσῆς]] [[otherwise|otherwise, but, except, yet, but then and however, but really and certainly|ἀλλά]] [[also|also and even, but, nay, and yet, as, likewise|καί]] you [[you will give|you will give, you will grant, you will provide, you will give over and deliver up|δίδωμι]] to us [[whole burnt-offerings|whole burnt-offerings and holocausts|ὁλοκαύτωμα]] and [[offerings|offerings, modes of offering, offerings and sacrifices and sacred rites, festivals, victims|θυσία]], which [[we will make|we will make, we will do, we will produce, we will create|ποιέω]] [[to lord|to lord, to master, to the one having power and authority over|κύριος]] [[to the God|to him who is God definitively, to the one the article marks out, to the known and the only|θεός]] of us,

greek: καὶ τὰ κτήνη ἡμῶν πορεύσεται μεθʼ ἡμῶν, καὶ οὐχ ὑπολειψόμεθα ὁπλήν· ἀπʼ αὐτῶν γὰρ λημψόμεθα λατρεῦσαι κυρίῳ τῷ θεῷ ἡμῶν· ἡμεῖς δὲ οὐκ οἴδαμεν, τί λατρεύσωμεν κυρίῳ τῷ θεῷ ἡμῶν, ἕως τοῦ ἐλθεῖν ἡμᾶς ἐκεῖ.
hint: Moses says the livestock go too, not a hoof left, since they will not know what to offer until they arrive.

notes.text: We will not leave a hoof behind, first person: the Hebrew has lōʾ tiššāʾēr parsâ, not a hoof will be left.
Until we come, the articular infinitive in the genitive after ἕως.

reading: and [[the flocks and herds|the flocks and herds, the single beasts, the beasts for riding|κτῆνος]] of us [[will be driven|will be driven, will be carried, will go, will walk, will march, will go across and pass|πορεύομαι]] [[in the midst of|in the midst of, among, in common, along with, with, by means of|μετά + genitive]] of us, and not [[we will leave remaining for ourselves|we will leave remaining for ourselves, we will leave behind for ourselves, we will reserve for ourselves|ὑπολείπω]] [[a hoof|a hoof and solid hoof, cloven hoof|ὁπλή]]; [[from|from, away from, far from, apart from|ἀπό]] of them [[for|for, since and as, for otherwise and else, now, but, why and what, would that|γάρ]], [[we will take|we will take, we will receive, we will take hold of and grasp and seize|λαμβάνω]] [[to work for hire|to work for hire and pay and be in servitude and serve, to be bound and enslaved to, to serve, to obey, to render due|λατρεύω]] [[to lord|to lord, to master, to the one having power and authority over|κύριος]] [[to the God|to him who is God definitively, to the one the article marks out, to the known and the only|θεός]] of us; we [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], not [[we know|we know, we are assured, we are versed in|οἶδα]], what [[we may work for hire|we may work for hire and pay and be in servitude and serve, we may be bound and enslaved to, we may serve, we may obey, we may render due|λατρεύω]] [[to lord|to lord, to master, to the one having power and authority over|κύριος]] [[to the God|to him who is God definitively, to the one the article marks out, to the known and the only|θεός]] of us, [[until|until, till, while and so long as|ἕως]] [[of the coming|of the coming, of the going, of the going back and returning, of the being going to and intending, of the coming within a little of and being near|ἔρχομαι]] us [[there|there, in that place|ἐκεῖ]].

greek: ἐσκλήρυνεν δὲ κύριος τὴν καρδίαν Φαραω, καὶ οὐκ ἐβουλήθη ἐξαποστεῖλαι αὐτούς.
hint: The lord hardens Pharaoh's heart, and he refuses to release them.

notes.text: The passive aorist of the deponent βούλομαι, active in sense: willed.

reading: hardened [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[lord|lord, master, the one having power and authority over|κύριος]] [[the heart|the heart, the stomach|καρδία]] of [[name:Φαραω]], and not [[willed|willed, wished and was willing, meant, professed and pretended and would fain, preferred|βούλομαι]] [[to send quite away|to send quite away, to dispatch|ἐξαποστέλλω]] them.

greek: καὶ λέγει Φαραω Ἄπελθε ἀπʼ ἐμοῦ, πρόσεχε σεαυτῷ ἔτι προσθεῖναι ἰδεῖν μου τὸ πρόσωπον· ᾗ δʼ ἂν ἡμέρᾳ ὀφθῇς μοι, ἀποθανῇ.
hint: Pharaoh orders Moses out and warns him that on the day he appears before him again he will die.

notes.lemma: ᾗ δʼ ἂν ἡμέρᾳ ὀφθῇς μοι
notes.text: On whatever day you are seen by me, the passive: the Hebrew has bĕyôm rĕʾōtĕkā pānay, on the day you see my face.
Take heed to yourself to add again, προστίθημι with the infinitive, to do again.

reading: and [[says|says, speaks, declares, calls by name, tells|λέγω]] [[name:Φαραω]] [[go away|go away, depart from, depart, depart from life|ἀπέρχομαι]] [[from|from, away from, far from, apart from|ἀπό]] of me, [[hold to|hold to and offer, bring to, turn to, turn the mind to, give heed to|προσέχω]] to yourself [[yet|yet, as yet, still, further, besides, moreover|ἔτι]] [[to put to|to put to, to hand over and deliver, to give and bestow, to impose further, to attribute, to add|προστίθημι]] [[to see|to see, to perceive, to behold, to look at|ὁράω]] of me [[the face|the face and visage and countenance, the look, the mask, the outward appearance|πρόσωπον]]; to which [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], ever [[to day|to day, to day-break, to time|ἡμέρα]] [[you may be seen|you may be seen, you may be looked at, you may be beheld and perceived and observed, you may be looked out for|ὁράω]] to me, [[you will die off|you will die off and die, you will be put to death and slain|ἀποθνήσκω]].

greek: λέγει δὲ Μωυσῆς Εἴρηκας· οὐκέτι ὀφθήσομαί σοι εἰς πρόσωπον.
hint: Moses replies that it is as Pharaoh has said: he will not appear before him again.

notes.text: You have said: the Hebrew has kēn dibbartā, you have spoken rightly.
No more will I be seen by you to the face, the passive: the Hebrew has lōʾ-ʾōsip ʿôd rĕʾôt pānêkā, I will not see your face again.

reading: [[says|says, speaks, declares, calls by name, tells|λέγω]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[name:Μωυσῆς]] [[you have said|you have said and it stands said, you have spoken and it stands spoken, you have declared and it stands declared, you have called by name and it stands so, you have told and it stands told|λέγω]]; [[no more|no more and no longer and no further|οὐκέτι]] [[I will be seen|I will be seen, I will be looked at, I will be beheld and perceived and observed, I will be looked out for|ὁράω]] to you [[into|into, to, in, rest in|εἰς]] [[face|face and visage and countenance, look, mask, outward appearance|πρόσωπον]].
